answer: Roots under mushrooms give the forest away. Stop reading names and read the graph: accounts that fund one another, share one pulse of timing, or answer each other like a zephyr curling back to its own leaves are single clusters in costume. A sybil farmer mints addresses cheaply but cannot mint edges - true neighbours cost months of money and attention. So judge the ember at the centre: trace co-funded treasuries, synchronized attestation bursts, and mutual upvote rings, then collapse each cluster to one voice. Bots buy nodes; they must still grow a graph, and graphs refuse to be rushed.
